miniProject.title: Exact planning oracles for small finite MDPs
miniProject.brief: Build the `policylab` foundation: versioned transition records, small finite MDPs and exact planning oracles that later samplers and networks must match. The project turns Bellman equations into tested code with seeded defects, so every later learning claim has an exact reference.
steps: Create `policylab` with `schema/`, `envs/`, `oracles/`, `tabular/`, `deep/`, `offline/`, `mbrl/`, `llm/`, `agents/`, `systems/`, `eval/`, `ledger/`, `faults/`, `tests/` and `reports/`, and record one versioned transition schema plus a small finite MDP with known dynamics in `envs/`.

Implement matrix-form exact evaluation and synchronous iterative evaluation in `oracles/`, prove their agreement on your MDP, and run the same oracle through the Stanford CS234 Assignment 1 `bellman_backup` and `policy_evaluation` functions on RiverSwim.

Implement policy iteration and value iteration with a fixed tie rule, check policy against value agreement on RiverSwim, pass Deep-ML 467, Deep-ML 157 and Deep-ML 164, and set the stopping tolerance from the residual over \(1 - \gamma\) rather than a fixed sweep count.

Seed tie-switching, unreachable-state and terminal-bootstrap defects in `faults/`, show each failing test before its repair, and prove truncation still bootstraps while true termination cuts the target.

Write the MDP contract with state sufficiency, action authority, reward components, termination, discount and evaluation policy, then seed one reward or terminal defect and keep a reward-hacking probe where the proxy optimum differs from the intended behavior.

Evaluate the greedy policy on several held-out seed streams with no training exploration, keep per-seed raw records in `ledger/` and `reports/`, and state what the optimal-policy claim does and does not establish.
deliverables: The `policylab` layout with the versioned schema, finite MDPs and exact planning oracles.
Tests: oracle agreement, RiverSwim policy and value match, residual stopping and seeded defect regressions.
The MDP contract with the evaluation policy, hacking probe and multi-seed greedy evaluation report.

checks.name: Deep-ML 467: Policy Iteration for MDPs
checks.note: Pass closed-book first; use as the policy iteration agreement check.

checks.name: Deep-ML 157: Bellman Update for Value Iteration
checks.note: Pass closed-book first; use as the value iteration backup check.

checks.name: Deep-ML 164: Gambler Value Iteration
checks.note: Match the spot values; use it as the episodic, undiscounted value-iteration check.

checks.name: Stanford CS234 Assignment 1 starter code
checks.note: Run Bellman backup and policy evaluation on RiverSwim from NumPy only.

rubric.pass: Iterative evaluation matches the matrix solve on your MDP, and policy and value iteration agree on RiverSwim.
rubric.strong: Agreement holds under several sweep orders and tie rules, with the residual bound predicting the remaining error.

rubric.pass: Tolerance comes from the residual bound, and values and policy convergence are reported separately.
rubric.strong: A premature stop is shown to leave value error while the policy looks stable, or the reverse.

rubric.pass: Each seeded tie, terminal and reward defect fails before its repair and passes after.
rubric.strong: One defect survives a naive fix and needs a second repair with its own regression test.

rubric.pass: The contract names the evaluation policy, and the hacking probe shows the proxy optimum missing the intent.
rubric.strong: Two competing formulations predict different optimal policies, and evaluation separates them.

miniProject.feedsInto: Exact MDPs, versioned records, planning oracles and defect discipline feed sampling, deep value and policy projects and the capstone classical core.
